Bug_Details:
Integer literals should not start with zero since this denotes that the rest of literal will be
interpreted as an octal value.
Examples:
int i = 012;    // set i with 10 not 12
int j = 010;    // set j with 8 not 10
k = i * j;      // set k with 80 not 120
Bug_Explanation: The bug here is the use of Octal numbers in integer literals. In Java, integer literals starting with a zero are interpreted as octal values, which means they are base 8. This can lead to unexpected results especially when the digits in the literal are greater than 7. For example, 012 in octal is 10 in decimal, not 12. Similarly, 010 is 8 in decimal, not 10.
